records.source: ה֣וֹי שׁוֹדֵ֗ד וְאַתָּה֙ לֹ֣א שָׁד֔וּד וּבוֹגֵ֖ד וְלֹא־בָ֣גְדוּ ב֑וֹ כַּהֲתִֽמְךָ֤ שׁוֹדֵד֙ תּוּשַּׁ֔ד כַּנְּלֹתְךָ֥ לִבְגֹּ֖ד יִבְגְּדוּ־בָֽךְ׃ס
records.gloss: Woe, destroyer, and you not destroyed, and treacherous one, and not they dealt treacherously with him; when you finish destroying you will be destroyed; when you complete dealing treacherously they will deal treacherously with you.
pieces: Woe to you, destroyer, never yet destroyed yourself, \q and you who deal falsely, though no one has dealt falsely with you! \q Once your destroying is done, you will be destroyed; \q once you finish your treachery, others will deal treacherously with you.

L.1: Woe, destroyer, [you who are] not destroyed, \q and treacherous one, [with whom] they have not dealt treacherously! \q When you finish destroying, you will be destroyed; \q when you complete dealing treacherously, they will deal treacherously with you.

R.1: How terrible it will be for you, destroyer! You destroy others, but no one has destroyed you. \q You betray others, but no one has betrayed you. \q When you finish destroying, you will be destroyed. \q When you stop betraying, others will betray you.

decisions.choice: the destroyer and the treacherous one: an unnamed enemy power, most likely Assyria
decisions.reason: The enemy is not named. Chapters 28-32 and 36-37 deal with the Assyrian threat to Jerusalem; Sennacherib took Hezekiah's payment and still sent his army against the city (2 Kings 18:13-17), which fits the charge of treachery. The same pair of words describes a destroyer in 21:2.

decisions.choice: when you finish ... you will be destroyed: the punishment will match the crime
decisions.reason: Each verb returns on the one who did it: the destroyer is destroyed and the betrayer is betrayed. The plural "they will deal treacherously" has no stated subject; it means others in general.

decisions.choice: others
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable supply "others" for the unstated plural subject.

records.heading: Woe to the destroyer

records.source: יְהוָ֥ה חָנֵּ֖נוּ לְךָ֣ קִוִּ֑ינוּ הֱיֵ֤ה זְרֹעָם֙ לַבְּקָרִ֔ים אַף־יְשׁוּעָתֵ֖נוּ בְּעֵ֥ת צָרָֽה׃
records.gloss: O Yahweh, be gracious to us; for you we have waited; be their arm in the mornings, also our salvation in a time of distress.
pieces: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, show us grace; we have waited for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. \q Be their strong arm morning by morning, \q and our salvation when trouble comes.

L.2: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, be gracious to us; for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} we have waited. \q Be their arm every morning, \q also our salvation in [the] time of distress.

R.2: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, be kind to us. We have been waiting for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} to help us. \q Be the strength of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people every morning. \q Save us when we are in trouble.

decisions.choice: their arm: the Hebrew text says "their", though the prayer speaks of "us" and "our"
decisions.reason: The shift from "us" to "their" is abrupt, and some ancient translations have "our arm". The Hebrew may mean the people the speakers pray for, or the leaders or fighters among them. Either way the arm stands for strength and help (40:10; 51:9).

decisions.choice: in the mornings: every morning, day after day
decisions.reason: Morning was when help was looked for after a night of danger (17:14; 37:36; Psalm 46:6). The plural means each new morning.

decisions.choice: the strength of your people
decisions.reason: Readable explains the arm as strength and keeps the third person by naming the people as God's.

records.heading: A prayer in a time of distress

records.source: מִקּ֣וֹל הָמ֔וֹן נָדְד֖וּ עַמִּ֑ים מֵר֣וֹמְמֻתֶ֔ךָ נָפְצ֖וּ גּוֹיִֽם׃
records.gloss: From the sound of tumult peoples fled; from your rising up nations were scattered.
pieces: At the roar of the uproar the peoples run; \q when {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} rise up, the nations scatter.

L.3: At [the] sound of tumult peoples flee; \q at {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} rising up nations are scattered.

R.3: When {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} thunder, whole nations run away. \q When {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} stand up to fight, the nations scatter.

decisions.choice: the sound of tumult: the roar of God's coming, like thunder
alternatives: the noise of the attacking armies
decisions.reason: Read with "your rising up", the noise belongs to God acting against the nations, as his voice thunders against Assyria in 30:30-31.

decisions.choice: they flee ... they were scattered: past forms describing what is certain to happen
decisions.reason: The verbs are perfect, but the prayer looks ahead to God's help; the prophets often speak of what God will surely do as already done.

decisions.choice: When you thunder
decisions.reason: Readable names the sound as God's own, as decision m1 explains.

records.source: וְאֻסַּ֣ף שְׁלַלְכֶ֔ם אֹ֖סֶף הֶֽחָסִ֑יל כְּמַשַּׁ֥ק גֵּבִ֖ים שׁוֹקֵ֥ק בּֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And your plunder will be gathered, the gathering of the caterpillar; like the rushing of locusts rushing on it.
pieces: Your spoil is swept up as caterpillars strip a field; \q like a swarm of locusts people rush upon it.

L.4: And your plunder will be gathered [as] the caterpillar gathers; \q like [the] rushing of locusts [people] rush upon it.

R.4: Nations, everything you stole will be taken away. People will grab it like caterpillars eating up a field. \q They will rush at it like a swarm of locusts.

decisions.choice: your plunder: the loot the enemy nations had taken, now taken from them
decisions.reason: "Your" is plural and speaks to the nations of verse 3. What they had seized is gathered up by others, as in 33:23.

decisions.choice: caterpillar ... locusts: insects that strip a land bare
decisions.reason: Locust swarms in their different stages could eat every green thing in a field (Joel 1:4). The picture is of plunder taken completely and fast.

decisions.choice: people
decisions.reason: The participle "rushing" has no stated subject; Literal brackets "people" and the other levels supply it.

decisions.choice: Nations, everything you stole
decisions.reason: Readable names whom the plural "your" addresses.

records.source: נִשְׂגָּ֣ב יְהוָ֔ה כִּ֥י שֹׁכֵ֖ן מָר֑וֹם מִלֵּ֣א צִיּ֔וֹן מִשְׁפָּ֖ט וּצְדָקָֽה׃
records.gloss: Exalted [is] Yahweh, for dwelling [on] high; he has filled Zion [with] justice and righteousness.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is exalted, for {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} lives on high; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will fill Zion with justice and righteousness.

L.5: Exalted [is] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, for {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} dwells [on] high; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has filled Zion [with] justice and righteousness.

R.5: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is greater than all. He lives in heaven above. \q He will fill Zion with fairness and with what is right.

decisions.choice: high place: the height of heaven where God reigns
decisions.reason: The word means height; with "dwelling" it points to God's throne above the earth (57:15; Psalm 113:5).

decisions.choice: he has filled: what God will surely do, spoken as done
decisions.reason: The perfect verb sits among promises about the future (verse 6); it states what God will certainly do for Zion.

decisions.choice: fairness and with what is right
decisions.reason: Readable spells out justice and righteousness in plain words.

records.source: וְהָיָה֙ אֱמוּנַ֣ת עִתֶּ֔יךָ חֹ֥סֶן יְשׁוּעֹ֖ת חָכְמַ֣ת וָדָ֑עַת יִרְאַ֥ת יְהוָ֖ה הִ֥יא אוֹצָרֽוֹ׃ס
records.gloss: And he will be the steadiness of your times, a wealth of deliverances, wisdom and knowledge; the fear of Yahweh, it [is] his treasure.
pieces: He will be the firm foundation of your times, \q a rich store of salvation, of wisdom and knowledge; \q the fear of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is his treasure.

L.6: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will be the stability of your times, \q a wealth of salvation, wisdom and knowledge; \q the fear of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, it [is] his treasure.

R.6: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will keep you safe all your life. \q He will give you a great supply of help, wisdom, and knowledge. \q Respecting {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will be your greatest treasure.

decisions.choice: the steadiness of your times: the one who makes your days secure
decisions.reason: The word means firmness and faithfulness. God himself is the steady ground of Zion's life in every season. "Your" is singular and speaks to Zion or her people as one.

decisions.choice: his treasure: the treasure of the people of Zion, spoken of as one person
decisions.reason: The pronoun is singular and masculine. It most likely refers to the people addressed as "your", whose true wealth is the fear of the LORD. It may instead mean the treasure God values most.

decisions.choice: your greatest treasure
decisions.reason: Readable follows decision m2 and uses "your", as earlier in the verse, for the same people.

decisions.choice: The LORD
decisions.reason: Readable names the subject of "he will be" from verse 5.

records.source: הֵ֚ן אֶרְאֶלָּ֔ם צָעֲק֖וּ חֻ֑צָה מַלְאֲכֵ֣י שָׁל֔וֹם מַ֖ר יִבְכָּיֽוּן׃
records.gloss: Look, their valiant ones have cried outside; messengers of peace weep bitterly.
pieces: Listen! Their brave warriors cry out in the streets; \q the envoys sent for peace weep bitter tears.

L.7: Look, their valiant ones cry out outside; \q [the] messengers of peace weep bitterly.

R.7: Listen! Brave soldiers are crying out in the streets. \q The men sent to ask for peace are crying bitterly.

decisions.choice: their valiant ones: their heroes or warriors
decisions.reason: This rare word is uncertain. It may be linked to a word for heroes (2 Samuel 23:20), or read as "Ariel", the name for Jerusalem in 29:1-2 ("I will appear to them" is another proposal). The sense "heroes" fits the parallel line.

decisions.choice: messengers of peace: envoys sent to make terms with the enemy
decisions.reason: Hezekiah sent word to Sennacherib and paid him heavily to withdraw (2 Kings 18:14-16), yet the Assyrian army still came. Their weeping shows the treaty has failed (verse 8).

decisions.choice: Listen!
decisions.reason: The particle calls attention; what follows is heard, a cry, so Balanced and Readable say "Listen".

records.source: נָשַׁ֣מּוּ מְסִלּ֔וֹת שָׁבַ֖ת עֹבֵ֣ר אֹ֑רַח הֵפֵ֤ר בְּרִית֙ מָאַ֣ס עָרִ֔ים לֹ֥א חָשַׁ֖ב אֱנֽוֹשׁ׃
records.gloss: Highways have been made desolate; the passer-by on the road has ceased; he has broken covenant; he has rejected cities; he has not valued man.
pieces: The highways lie empty; no traveler walks the road. \q He has broken the treaty and scorned the cities; he has no regard for human life.

L.8: [The] highways are desolate; [the] traveler on [the] road has ceased. \q He has broken [the] covenant; he has despised cities; he has not regarded humankind.

R.8: The roads are empty. No one travels on them anymore. \q The enemy has broken his agreement. He hates the cities. He does not care about people at all.

decisions.choice: cities: the Hebrew text has "cities"; the Great Isaiah Scroll has "witnesses"
decisions.reason: In Hebrew the two words differ by one similar letter. "Witnesses" would fit a broken covenant, since agreements were sealed before witnesses; "cities" fits the enemy's contempt for the towns he takes. The traditional Hebrew text is followed.

decisions.choice: covenant: the treaty between Judah and the enemy
decisions.reason: The word here is a political agreement, not God's covenant; it is the destroyer of verse 1 who breaks it.

decisions.choice: The enemy
decisions.reason: Readable names the subject of "he has broken", the destroyer of verse 1.

records.source: אָבַ֤ל אֻמְלְלָה֙ אָ֔רֶץ הֶחְפִּ֥יר לְבָנ֖וֹן קָמַ֑ל הָיָ֤ה הַשָּׁרוֹן֙ כָּֽעֲרָבָ֔ה וְנֹעֵ֥ר בָּשָׁ֖ן וְכַרְמֶֽל׃
records.gloss: The land has dried up, has languished; Lebanon has been ashamed, has withered; Sharon has become like the Arabah, and shaking off [are] Bashan and Carmel.
pieces: The land dries up and wastes away; Lebanon is put to shame and withers. \q Sharon is like the desert plain, and Bashan and Carmel drop their leaves.

L.9: [The] land mourns [and] languishes; Lebanon is ashamed [and] withers; \q Sharon has become like the Arabah, and Bashan and Carmel shake off [their leaves].

R.9: The land is drying up and dying. The forests of Lebanon are dried up. \q The rich fields of Sharon are like a desert. The trees of Bashan and Mount Carmel are losing their leaves.

decisions.choice: dried up: the land mourns and dries out
decisions.reason: The verb can mean "mourn" or "dry up"; both senses fit a land stripped by war and drought (24:4).

decisions.choice: Lebanon, Sharon, Bashan, Carmel: the most fertile places in the land
decisions.reason: Lebanon's forests, the plain of Sharon, the pastures and oaks of Bashan, and the slopes of Carmel stood for richness and growth (35:2). Even they now look like the Arabah, the dry rift valley.

decisions.choice: their leaves
decisions.reason: The verb means "shake off"; what is shaken off is understood: the trees' leaves.

records.source: עַתָּ֥ה אָק֖וּם יֹאמַ֣ר יְהוָ֑ה עַתָּה֙ אֵֽרוֹמָ֔ם עַתָּ֖ה אֶנָּשֵֽׂא׃
records.gloss: Now I will arise, says Yahweh; now I will be exalted; now I will lift myself up.
pieces: Now I will rise up, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; \q now I will show {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}} high and mighty; now I will lift {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}} up.

L.10: Now I will arise, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; \q now I will exalt {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}}; now I will lift {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}} up.

R.10: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} says, Now I will get up and act. \q Now I will show how great I am. Now I will show {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} power.

decisions.choice: now ... now ... now: the moment for God to act has come
decisions.reason: The threefold "now" answers the prayer of verse 2 and the ruin of verses 7-9. God rises as a warrior rises to battle (2:19, 21).

decisions.choice: I will exalt myself ... I will lift myself up: God takes the high place proud people claimed
decisions.reason: The same words describe the LORD in 6:1 and 52:13 and stand against the pride brought low in 2:12-17. Verse 5 has already said the LORD is exalted.

decisions.choice: The LORD says, Now ...
decisions.reason: Readable puts the speaker first so the reader knows at once who is speaking.

records.source: תַּהֲר֥וּ חֲשַׁ֖שׁ תֵּ֣לְדוּ קַ֑שׁ רוּחֲכֶ֕ם אֵ֖שׁ תֹּאכַלְכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: You will conceive dry grass; you will give birth to stubble; your breath [is] a fire [that] will consume you.
pieces: You are pregnant with chaff, and you give birth to straw; \q your own breath is a fire that will burn you up.

L.11: You conceive dry grass, you give birth to stubble; \q your breath [is] a fire [that] will consume you.

R.11: Your plans are as useless as dry grass and straw. \q Your own angry breath will be a fire that burns you up.

decisions.choice: conceive dry grass, give birth to stubble: plans that come to nothing
decisions.reason: "You" is plural and speaks to the enemy nations. Conceiving and bearing stand for making and carrying out plans (59:4; Psalm 7:15); what they bring forth is worthless and burns easily.

decisions.choice: your breath: the enemy's own fury and schemes
decisions.reason: Their own raging spirit becomes the fire that destroys them, so their ruin comes from themselves (compare 1:31). The word can also mean "spirit".

decisions.choice: Your plans are as useless as dry grass and straw
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture of conceiving and giving birth.

records.source: וְהָי֥וּ עַמִּ֖ים מִשְׂרְפ֣וֹת שִׂ֑יד קוֹצִ֥ים כְּסוּחִ֖ים בָּאֵ֥שׁ יִצַּֽתּוּ׃ס
records.gloss: And peoples will be burnings of lime; thorns cut down, with fire they will be kindled.
pieces: The peoples will be burned to lime, \q like thorns that are cut and set on fire.

L.12: And [the] peoples will be burnings of lime, \q thorns cut down [that] are set ablaze with fire.

R.12: The nations will be burned up until nothing is left but white ash. \q They will burn like thornbushes that are cut down and thrown into a fire.

decisions.choice: burnings of lime: fire so hot it turns stone or bone to powder
decisions.reason: Lime was made by burning limestone in a kiln until it crumbled to white powder. Burning bones to lime was a sign of complete destruction (Amos 2:1).

decisions.choice: until nothing is left but white ash
decisions.reason: Readable explains what burning to lime leaves behind.

records.source: שִׁמְע֥וּ רְחוֹקִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשִׂ֑יתִי וּדְע֥וּ קְרוֹבִ֖ים גְּבֻרָתִֽי׃
records.gloss: Hear, distant ones, what I have done, and know, near ones, my might.
pieces: You who are far away, hear what I have done; \q you who are near, acknowledge {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} strength.

L.13: Hear, [you who are] far away, what I have done; \q and know, [you who are] near, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} might.

R.13: Listen, you people who live far away. Hear what I have done. \q You people who live nearby, see how strong I am.

decisions.choice: distant ones ... near ones: all people, from the farthest nations to the people close at hand
decisions.reason: The pair takes in everyone (57:19). The nations far off and the people in Zion are both to recognize what God has done to the destroyer.

decisions.choice: know: recognize and acknowledge
decisions.reason: Knowing here means accepting the truth of God's power once it is seen, not only learning a fact.

records.heading: Who can live with the devouring fire?

records.source: פָּחֲד֤וּ בְצִיּוֹן֙ חַטָּאִ֔ים אָחֲזָ֥ה רְעָדָ֖ה חֲנֵפִ֑ים מִ֣י׀יָג֣וּר לָ֗נוּ אֵ֚שׁ אוֹכֵלָ֔ה מִי־יָג֥וּר לָ֖נוּ מוֹקְדֵ֥י עוֹלָֽם׃
records.gloss: They are in dread in Zion, sinners; trembling has seized the godless: who will sojourn for us [with] consuming fire? Who will sojourn for us [with] hearths of perpetuity?
pieces: The sinners in Zion are terrified; the godless are gripped by trembling: \q "Which of us can live as a guest beside the devouring fire? \q Which of us can stay where the burning lasts forever?"

L.14: [The] sinners in Zion are in dread; trembling has seized [the] godless: \q "Who among us can sojourn [with the] consuming fire? \q Who among us can sojourn [with] everlasting burnings?"

R.14: The sinners in Zion are afraid. People who reject God are shaking with fear. \q They ask, "Which of us can live near God, who is like a fire that destroys? \q Which of us can live near flames that never go out?"

decisions.choice: sojourn with the consuming fire: live in the presence of the holy God
alternatives: live through the fire of judgment on the enemy (verses 11-12)
decisions.reason: God is called a consuming fire (Deuteronomy 4:24; Isaiah 10:17; 30:27, 30). The question echoes Psalm 15:1 and 24:3, "Who may dwell on your holy hill?", and verses 15-16 give an answer like those psalms. To sojourn is to live as a guest under a host's protection.

decisions.choice: the godless: people who have turned from God
decisions.reason: The word describes those who are corrupt and faithless toward God, not only those who deny him (9:16; 10:6).

decisions.choice: near God, who is like a fire that destroys
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly that the fire stands for God, following decision m1.

decisions.choice: live as a guest ... stay
decisions.reason: Balanced brings out the verb's sense of living as a guest; Literal keeps "sojourn".

records.source: הֹלֵ֣ךְ צְדָק֔וֹת וְדֹבֵ֖ר מֵֽישָׁרִ֑ים מֹאֵ֞ס בְּבֶ֣צַע מַעֲשַׁקּ֗וֹת נֹעֵ֤ר כַּפָּיו֙ מִתְּמֹ֣ךְ בַּשֹּׁ֔חַד אֹטֵ֤ם אָזְנוֹ֙ מִשְּׁמֹ֣עַ דָּמִ֔ים וְעֹצֵ֥ם עֵינָ֖יו מֵרְא֥וֹת בְּרָֽע׃
records.gloss: One walking righteousnesses and speaking uprightnesses, rejecting gain of extortions, shaking his palms from holding on a bribe, shutting his ear from hearing bloods, and shutting his eyes from looking on evil,
pieces: Whoever lives by what is right and speaks honestly, \q whoever turns down profit squeezed from others, whose hands shake off a bribe instead of grasping it, \q whose ears are closed to talk of bloodshed, \q and whose eyes are shut against gazing at evil,

L.15: [The] one walking [in] righteousness and speaking uprightly, \q rejecting [the] gain of extortion, shaking his hands from holding a bribe, \q stopping his ears from hearing [of] bloodshed, \q and shutting his eyes from looking on evil,

R.15: The people who can live there are those who do what is right and speak the truth. \q They refuse to get rich by cheating others. They will not take bribes. \q They will not listen to plans to kill people. They will not look at evil things.

decisions.choice: the one walking in righteousness: the answer to the question of verse 14
decisions.reason: Like Psalm 15:2-5 and 24:4, the answer describes a person whose life is honest and just. It gives six marks, in deed, word, money, hands, ears and eyes.

decisions.choice: hearing bloods: listening to plots to shed blood
decisions.reason: The plural "bloods" means bloodshed or guilt for killing. The person refuses even to listen when violence is planned (Proverbs 1:11-16).

decisions.choice: Whoever ... whose hands / They
decisions.reason: The description fits anyone, man or woman. Balanced uses "whoever" and "whose", and Readable the plural "they", in place of the masculine singular pronouns that Literal keeps.

decisions.choice: The people who can live there are
decisions.reason: Readable states the link to the question of verse 14.

records.source: ה֚וּא מְרוֹמִ֣ים יִשְׁכֹּ֔ן מְצָד֥וֹת סְלָעִ֖ים מִשְׂגַּבּ֑וֹ לַחְמ֣וֹ נִתָּ֔ן מֵימָ֖יו נֶאֱמָנִֽים׃
records.gloss: He on heights will dwell; strongholds of cliffs his refuge; his bread given, his water sure.
pieces: that one will make a home on the heights, with fortresses of rock for refuge, \q with bread supplied and water that never fails.

L.16: he will dwell [on the] heights; strongholds of rocks [will be] his refuge; \q his bread [will be] given, his water [will be] sure.

R.16: They will live in high places where they are safe. Rocky fortresses will protect them. \q They will always have food to eat and water to drink.

decisions.choice: heights ... strongholds of cliffs: a safe place God provides
decisions.reason: Fortresses on rocky heights could not easily be taken. The person who lives with God is kept safe and supplied, even in a siege, when bread and water ran short (36:12).

decisions.choice: sure: reliable, never running dry
decisions.reason: The word is used of what is faithful and lasting; the water supply will not fail (compare 58:11).

decisions.choice: that one
decisions.reason: Balanced continues verse 15's "whoever" with "that one" in place of "he" (see 15:r-en-1).

records.source: מֶ֥לֶךְ בְּיָפְי֖וֹ תֶּחֱזֶ֣ינָה עֵינֶ֑יךָ תִּרְאֶ֖ינָה אֶ֥רֶץ מַרְחַקִּֽים׃
records.gloss: A king in his beauty your eyes will see; they will see a land of distances.
pieces: Your eyes will see a king in his splendor; \q they will look on a land that stretches far away.

L.17: A king in his beauty your eyes will see; \q they will see a land of far distances.

R.17: You will see the king in all his beauty. \q You will see a land that stretches out wide in every direction.

decisions.choice: a king in his beauty: either the LORD himself as king, or the righteous king of David's line
alternatives: a human king of David's line
decisions.reason: Verse 22 calls the LORD "our king", and Zion's people will see him reigning. But 32:1 promises a king who will reign in righteousness, and the faithful king of David's line is described in beauty in Psalm 45:3. The text does not settle which is meant.

decisions.choice: a land of distances: a wide land with open borders
decisions.reason: Under siege the people saw only their walls. Now they will see a broad land stretching into the distance, no longer hemmed in.

decisions.choice: the king
decisions.reason: Readable uses "the" for a king the readers know is coming; the Hebrew has no article.

records.source: לִבְּךָ֖ יֶהְגֶּ֣ה אֵימָ֑ה אַיֵּ֤ה סֹפֵר֙ אַיֵּ֣ה שֹׁקֵ֔ל אַיֵּ֖ה סֹפֵ֥ר אֶת־הַמִּגְדָּלִֽים׃
records.gloss: Your heart will meditate on terror: where [is] the counter? where [is] the weigher? where [is] the counter of the towers?
pieces: Your mind will think back on the terror: \q "Where is the clerk who counted? Where is the one who weighed out the tribute? \q Where is the officer who counted the towers?"

L.18: Your heart will muse on [the] terror: \q "Where [is the] one who counted? Where [is the] one who weighed? \q Where [is the] one who counted the towers?"

R.18: You will remember how afraid you were. \q You will say, "Where are the enemy officials who counted our money? Where are those who weighed out what we paid? \q Where are the officers who counted our towers?"

decisions.choice: the one who counted ... weighed ... counted the towers: officials of the occupying enemy
decisions.reason: The "one who counted" is a scribe. Foreign officials recorded and weighed the tribute (2 Kings 18:14) and surveyed the city's towers to plan an attack or set taxes. Now they are gone. Paul echoes these questions in 1 Corinthians 1:20.

decisions.choice: the tribute / what we paid
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what was weighed: silver paid as tribute (2 Kings 18:14).

decisions.choice: the enemy officials
decisions.reason: Readable says who these people were, following decision m1.

records.source: אֶת־עַ֥ם נוֹעָ֖ז לֹ֣א תִרְאֶ֑ה עַ֣ם עִמְקֵ֤י שָׂפָה֙ מִשְּׁמ֔וֹעַ נִלְעַ֥ג לָשׁ֖וֹן אֵ֥ין בִּינָֽה׃
records.gloss: The people barbarous you will not see, a people deep of lip from hearing, stammering of tongue, no understanding.
pieces: You will no longer see that fierce nation, \q a people whose speech is too strange to follow, whose stammering tongue makes no sense to you.

L.19: The insolent people you will not see, \q a people of speech too deep to hear, of stammering tongue [that has] no understanding.

R.19: You will not see those cruel foreigners anymore. \q You will not hear their strange language that you could not understand.

decisions.choice: barbarous: fierce, insolent
decisions.reason: The word occurs only here. It is usually linked to a root meaning "be strong" or "be bold", describing a fierce and arrogant foe.

decisions.choice: deep of lip, stammering of tongue: a foreign language Judah could not understand
decisions.reason: God warned that he would speak to his people through foreigners with stammering lips and a strange tongue (28:11; Deuteronomy 28:49). The occupiers whose speech sounded like nonsense will be gone.

records.source: חֲזֵ֣ה צִיּ֔וֹן קִרְיַ֖ת מֽוֹעֲדֵ֑נוּ עֵינֶיךָ֩ תִרְאֶ֨ינָה יְרוּשָׁלִַ֜ם נָוֶ֣ה שַׁאֲנָ֗ן אֹ֤הֶל בַּל־יִצְעָן֙ בַּל־יִסַּ֤ע יְתֵֽדֹתָיו֙ לָנֶ֔צַח וְכָל־חֲבָלָ֖יו בַּל־יִנָּתֵֽקוּ׃
records.gloss: See Zion, town of our appointed feast; your eyes will see Jerusalem, habitation undisturbed, a tent [that] not will be packed up; not will be pulled out its pegs forever, and all its ropes not will be torn apart.
pieces: Look at Zion, the city where we keep our festivals! \q Your eyes will see Jerusalem, a home at rest, a tent that will never be taken down. Its pegs will never be pulled up, \q and not one of its ropes will snap.

L.20: See Zion, [the] city of our appointed feasts; \q your eyes will see Jerusalem, an untroubled dwelling, a tent [that] will not be packed up; its pegs will never be pulled out, \q and none of its ropes will be snapped.

R.20: Look at Zion, the city where we gather to worship at the festivals! \q You will see Jerusalem as a calm and peaceful place to live. It will be like a tent that will never be moved. Its pegs will never be pulled up. \q Its ropes will never break.

decisions.choice: town of our appointed feast: Jerusalem as the place of Israel's sacred festivals
decisions.reason: The word means an appointed time or gathering. The pilgrim festivals were kept at Jerusalem (Deuteronomy 16:16), and the city at peace will keep them again.

decisions.choice: a tent that will not be packed up: a home that will never again be uprooted
decisions.reason: The picture recalls the tent of meeting in the wilderness, which was taken down at every move. Jerusalem will be settled for good (54:2).

records.source: כִּ֣י אִם־שָׁ֞ם אַדִּ֤יר יְהוָה֙ לָ֔נוּ מְקוֹם־נְהָרִ֥ים יְאֹרִ֖ים רַחֲבֵ֣י יָדָ֑יִם בַּל־תֵּ֤לֶךְ בּוֹ֙ אֳנִי־שַׁ֔יִט וְצִ֥י אַדִּ֖יר לֹ֥א יַעַבְרֶֽנּוּ׃
records.gloss: But there majestic Yahweh for us, a place of rivers, canals broad of both hands; not will go on it a ship of oar, and a ship majestic not will pass along it.
pieces: Instead, there {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} in majesty will be ours, \q a place of rivers and wide streams, \q where no galley with oars will sail \q and no mighty ship will pass through.

L.21: But there {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [will be] majestic for us, \q a place of rivers, of streams broad on both sides, \q where no galley with oars will go, \q and no majestic ship will pass.

R.21: There {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will show us {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} greatness. \q He will be like wide rivers and streams around us. \q But no enemy warships will sail on them to attack us.

decisions.choice: a place of rivers: the LORD himself will be to Jerusalem what great rivers are to other cities
decisions.reason: Jerusalem had no river. Cities like Thebes and Nineveh were guarded by water (Nahum 3:8), and the LORD will be that protection. Compare the river that gladdens the city of God (Psalm 46:5).

decisions.choice: a ship of oar ... a majestic ship: warships
decisions.reason: A river can bring enemy fleets, but these rivers will carry no war galleys. The same word "majestic" is used for the LORD and for the ship: the only majesty in that place is God's.

decisions.choice: enemy warships ... to attack us
decisions.reason: Readable says what kind of ships are meant, following decision m2.

records.source: כִּ֤י יְהוָה֙ שֹׁפְטֵ֔נוּ יְהוָ֖ה מְחֹקְקֵ֑נוּ יְהוָ֥ה מַלְכֵּ֖נוּ ה֥וּא יוֹשִׁיעֵֽנוּ׃
records.gloss: For Yahweh [is] our judge; Yahweh [is] our commander; Yahweh [is] our king; he will deliver us.
pieces: For our judge is {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, our lawgiver is {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q our king is {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} will save us.

L.22: For {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [is] our judge, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [is] our lawgiver, \q {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [is] our king; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will save us.

R.22: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is the one who judges us. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} gives us our laws. \q {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is our king. He will save us.

decisions.choice: lawgiver: the one who decrees and rules
decisions.reason: The word comes from a verb meaning to inscribe or decree. It can mean the one who gives laws, or a ruler or commander (Genesis 49:10; Judges 5:14). Here, beside "judge" and "king", it names the LORD as the one who governs his people.

decisions.choice: Yahweh ... Yahweh ... Yahweh ... he: the LORD alone rules and rescues
decisions.reason: Judging, making law and ruling as king were the duties of a king in Israel. All three belong to the LORD, and the emphatic "he" stresses that he and no one else will save.

decisions.choice: our judge is the LORD
decisions.reason: Balanced puts each title first so the divine name ends each line with weight, and renders the emphatic pronoun "he himself".

records.source: נִטְּשׁ֖וּ חֲבָלָ֑יִךְ בַּל־יְחַזְּק֤וּ כֵן־תָּרְנָם֙ בַּל־פָּ֣רְשׂוּ נֵ֔ס אָ֣ז חֻלַּ֤ק עַֽד־שָׁלָל֙ מַרְבֶּ֔ה פִּסְחִ֖ים בָּ֥זְזוּ בַֽז׃
records.gloss: They hang loose, your ropes; not they make firm the base of their mast, not they spread out a sail; then will be divided booty of plunder in abundance; lame ones will take spoil.
pieces: Your ropes hang slack; \q they cannot hold the mast firm in its socket or spread out the sail. \q Then plunder will be shared out in heaps, \q and even the lame will carry off spoil.

L.23: Your ropes hang loose; \q they do not hold the base of their mast firm; they do not spread [the] sail. \q Then booty of plunder will be divided in abundance; \q [the] lame will take [the] spoil.

R.23: Enemy, you are like a ship whose ropes are loose. \q The ropes cannot hold up the mast. The sail cannot be raised. \q Then all your treasure will be divided up. \q There will be so much that even people who cannot walk well will carry some away.

decisions.choice: your ropes hang loose: the enemy pictured as a ship that cannot sail
decisions.reason: "Your" is singular and returns to the destroyer of verse 1. Following the rivers and warships of verse 21, the enemy is a ship falling apart. Some read it as Zion, weak now but about to share in the plunder.

decisions.choice: booty ... lame: the spoil is so great that even the weakest take a share
decisions.reason: The rare word for booty also occurs in Genesis 49:27. Normally the strong took the spoil; here even the lame do, because God won the victory, not Judah's soldiers.

decisions.choice: Enemy, you are like a ship
decisions.reason: Readable names the one addressed and states the comparison, following decision m1.

records.source: וּבַל־יֹאמַ֥ר שָׁכֵ֖ן חָלִ֑יתִי הָעָ֛ם הַיֹּשֵׁ֥ב בָּ֖הּ נְשֻׂ֥א עָוֺֽן׃
records.gloss: And not will say an inhabitant, I am sick; the people dwelling in it forgiven of iniquity.
pieces: No one who lives there will say, "I am sick"; \q the people who dwell in it will have their guilt forgiven.

L.24: And no inhabitant will say, "I am sick"; \q the people who dwell in it [will be] forgiven [their] iniquity.

R.24: No one who lives in Zion will say, "I am sick." \q God will forgive the sins of the people who live there.

decisions.choice: I am sick ... forgiven of iniquity: healing and forgiveness come together
decisions.reason: Sickness was a picture of the nation's sin and its results (1:5-6). The promise ends with God taking away guilt, the deepest need behind the city's suffering (40:2; 53:5).

decisions.choice: forgiven of iniquity: their iniquity is lifted away
decisions.reason: The verb means "lifted" or "carried": their guilt is removed. The passive leaves God as the one who forgives.

decisions.choice: God will forgive
decisions.reason: Readable names the one who forgives, which the passive verb implies.
